title: Log Analytics vs Application Insights
description: Decide where platform logs and application telemetry should live, and query them together.

data.text: Your team has Application Insights for the API, diagnostic settings flowing into a Log Analytics workspace, and a separate workspace created by the platform team. An incident starts with an App Service restart but the root cause is in firewall logs. Where should all this data live so one query explains the incident?

Use a **single Log Analytics workspace** as the data plane for both platform diagnostics and Application Insights. Application Insights should be created in **workspace-based mode** so its tables (`AppRequests`, `AppDependencies`, `AppTraces`) sit beside `AzureDiagnostics` and `AzureMetrics` in the same workspace. Then one Kusto query can join an App Service restart to a network security group denial.

data.title: Workspace-based Application Insights (Bicep)
Kusto query — join restart with firewall denial
data.code:
let restarts = AzureActivity
    | where OperationNameValue has "restart"
    | project restartTime = TimeGenerated, resource = ResourceId;
let denials = AzureDiagnostics
    | where Category == "AzureFirewallNetworkRule" and msg_s has "Deny"
    | project denyTime = TimeGenerated, source = SourceIP_s;
denials
| join kind=leftouter restarts on $left.denyTime == $right.restartTime
| where isnotempty(resource)
| project denyTime, source, resource

data.text: Separate workspaces make incident investigation a manual copy-paste exercise between portals. A shared workspace also lets you apply one **retention** and **access control** policy, and cross-resource queries (`app()`, `workspace()`) still work if a legal or regional boundary forces you to split.

cards.title: Single workspace (workspace-based App Insights)
cards.description: All telemetry in one queryable store
